clue.text: High flier?

parts.note: a high flier usually means an ambitious achiever, but here it is a tiny bird whose wings hum as it hovers

explanation.surface: Sounds like praise for an ambitious high-achiever.
explanation.walkthrough: The phrase 'high flier' normally describes a successful person; read literally it is any creature that flies, here a small hovering bird.
explanation.definitionFit: This tiny bird is a flier, the question mark admitting the stretch from a career sense to a literal one.

clue.text: Undersea menace could be about

indicators.note: the letters of the next word could be rearranged into something else, signalling a reshuffle

explanation.surface: A warning that something lurking beneath the sea might be nearby.
explanation.walkthrough: 'About' reads as 'nearby' in the surface, but its five letters are the fodder rearranged by 'could be'.
explanation.definitionFit: German submarines of the World Wars threatened Allied shipping from below the waves.

clue.text: Token note the French sent north

parts.note: a minim is a musical note, a half note

indicators.note: in a down clue, sending a word north means writing it upwards, i.e. backwards

parts.note: la is the French feminine word for 'the'

explanation.surface: Someone posts a token note northwards to a French recipient.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'sent north' means read upwards; the palindromic musical note stays the same, so only the French article flips.
explanation.definitionFit: A token gesture is one made with the smallest possible effort, so it is very slight.

clue.text: Ask again for change in Japanese city

indicators.note: asking for a change means the letters of the preceding words are altered into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone asks again for coins in exchange while visiting Japan.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for change' rearranges the eight letters of ASK AGAIN.
explanation.definitionFit: This port on Kyushu is the Japanese city struck by the second atomic bomb in 1945.

clue.text: Newsreader Bruce fine to leave Scottish island

indicators.note: the letter for fine is made to leave, i.e. is taken out of the name

parts.note: Fiona Bruce is a BBC newsreader and presenter
F is the abbreviation for fine, as on pencil grades

explanation.surface: A TV newsreader is happy to quit a Scottish isle.
explanation.walkthrough: Fiona Bruce is a well-known BBC news presenter; 'to leave' takes F from her first name.
explanation.definitionFit: This small Hebridean island off Mull is famed for St Columba's abbey.

clue.text: Scandalous amount taken in old window tax?

definitions.meaning: a blatant overcharge, an outrageous price exacted openly
the British window tax of 1696 to 1851 charged for windows, said to rob people of light, a folk origin of the phrase

explanation.surface: An outraged complaint about a historic tax on windows.
explanation.walkthrough: The window tax made householders brick up windows, so it 'stole' sunlight; the question mark flags this playful literal reading.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means being openly and outrageously overcharged, a theft committed in plain view.

clue.text: Dictator having a role in something contentious?

indicators.note: the pieces are placed in the contentious item, inside its letters

parts.note: a bone of contention is a contentious matter, so the clue hints at BONE
a part is an actor's role

explanation.surface: A dictator takes a role in a controversial affair.
explanation.walkthrough: 'something contentious?' leans on the idiom 'bone of contention', the question mark flagging the indirect hint; 'in' signals the container.
explanation.definitionFit: Napoleon seized absolute power in France, ruling as an emperor and autocrat.

clue.text: Dublin-born compiler's flame-haired companion?

parts.note: someone born in Dublin is Irish
a crossword compiler is called a setter

explanation.surface: A crossword maker from Dublin has a red-headed sidekick.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's is a link; the definition hints at the red coat of this breed of gun dog, a man's best friend.
explanation.definitionFit: This red-coated gun dog breed is a loyal pet, so a companion whose coat is the colour of flame.

clue.text: Mail perhaps won't feature first Republican affair

indicators.note: the first of the letters for Republican will not appear, so it is removed

parts.note: chain mail is a kind of armour

explanation.surface: A newspaper declines to run a story about a Republican's affair.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mail' looks like the newspaper but is chain mail; 'won't feature first' drops the first R of ARMOUR.
explanation.definitionFit: This French borrowing names a love affair, especially a secret or illicit romance.

clue.text: Saved having experienced the Second Coming?

definitions.meaning: spiritually redeemed, converted to evangelical faith
literally, having arrived in the world a second time, a playful take on the Christian term

explanation.surface: A believer who has lived through Christ's return.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Second Coming' suggests Christ's return; read literally it is being delivered into the world twice.
explanation.definitionFit: Evangelical Christians describe conversion as a spiritual rebirth, so converts are saved and renewed.

clue.text: Keen to gather complete cereal crop?

parts.note: all means the complete amount, everything
ears are the seed heads of cereal plants such as wheat

explanation.surface: A farmer eager to harvest an entire field of grain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gather' suggests harvest but here means gather information, by listening.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone listening intently is eager to take in every detail they hear.

clue.text: Storm in Timor Sea that generates spray

indicators.note: to storm is to rage violently, tossing the letters of the following words into disorder

explanation.surface: A storm over the Timor Sea whipping up spray.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Storm' is the anagram signal on the letters of TIMOR SEA.
explanation.definitionFit: A perfume or medicine device turns liquid into a fine mist of droplets.

clue.text: Bread requested for starters?

parts.note: bread is slang for money, and this is the money a seller requests at the start of haggling

explanation.surface: A diner asks for bread to be served as an appetiser.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bread' is slang for money and 'starters' means opening bids, not the first course of a meal.
explanation.definitionFit: A seller's opening figure is the sum of money they first request before any negotiation.

clue.text: Charged again in hearing — that's put back up

indicators.note: the words are judged as they would be heard, by their sound

parts.note: billed a second time, re-billed

explanation.surface: A defendant facing fresh charges in court.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Charged' and 'hearing' suggest a court case, but 'in hearing' signals that RE-BILLED is said aloud.
explanation.definitionFit: To reconstruct something knocked down is to erect it once more.

clue.text: Watch golf with girl: singular spectacle?

parts.note: to eye something is to watch it
G is golf in the NATO phonetic alphabet
a lass is a girl

explanation.surface: Spectating a round of golf with a girlfriend is quite a sight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spectacle' is a pair of glasses; singular, it is a single lens.
explanation.definitionFit: A monocle is one lens, so it is a lone version of a pair of glasses.

clue.text: Chancellor once in black eyeliner

definitions.meaning: Helmut ... was Chancellor of Germany from 1982 to 1998
a dark powder used to line the eyes

explanation.surface: A former political leader seen wearing dark eye make-up.
explanation.definitionFit: One sense is the German statesman who reunified his country; the other a traditional dark cosmetic powder.

clue.text: Pulse right to coat in warm batter

indicators.note: the letter for right is coated, enclosed in the word for warm

parts.note: to warm something is to heat it
to batter is to beat

explanation.surface: Cooking instructions for coating food in warm batter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'batter' looks culinary but means beat; 'to coat in' puts R inside HEAT.
explanation.definitionFit: A pulse is a single throb of the heart, felt at the wrist.

clue.text: Very good designer is provocative

parts.note: PI is short for pious, very good morally
Mary Quant was the British fashion designer who popularised the miniskirt

explanation.surface: A top fashion designer whose work is daring.
explanation.walkthrough: PI (pious) is a crossword staple for 'very good'; Mary Quant was a 1960s London fashion designer.
explanation.definitionFit: Something piquant stimulates interest, being pleasantly sharp, racy or stimulating.

clue.text: Ancient vampire rowing on lake

indicators.note: rowing here is a quarrel, a ruckus that throws the letters of the word into disorder

explanation.surface: A vampire rowing a boat across a lake at night.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rowing' looks like oarsmanship but is read as arguing, signalling the anagram of VAMPIRE.
explanation.definitionFit: Primeval things belong to the earliest ages of the world, so they are very old.

clue.text: Recruits down below almost lost

indicators.note: lost means confused and astray, so the letters wander into a new order
almost all of the word, the last letter being cut off

explanation.surface: Morale among recruits in the lower ranks has nearly gone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'almost' trims BELOW to BELO; 'lost' then rearranges DOWN plus BELO.
explanation.definitionFit: Fresh members joining an organisation bring vigour, like a transfusion of energy.

clue.text: Hit hard getting boxing prize

definitions.meaning: a championship strap awarded to a title-winning boxer

explanation.surface: A boxer wins a title by punching hard.
explanation.definitionFit: One sense is a verb for striking someone forcefully; the other the championship strap a boxer wins.

clue.text: Stolen meat comes to philosopher

parts.note: bent is slang for stolen or crooked
ham is a cured meat

explanation.surface: A thief brings stolen meat to a thinker.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bent' as British slang for stolen or dishonest is common in crosswords.
explanation.definitionFit: Jeremy Bentham was the English thinker who founded utilitarianism.

clue.text: Girl with name to conjure with in Zola's book

indicators.note: a name to conjure with is famous, but here the letters are conjured, magicked into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A famous woman's name appears in a Zola novel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a name to conjure with' is an idiom for a celebrated name; here 'to conjure with' rearranges GIRL and NAME.
explanation.definitionFit: Emile Zola's 1885 novel about a coal miners' strike bears this title.

clue.text: Suave and refined socialite currently broadcasting?

parts.note: a deb, short for debutante, is a young upper-class woman entering society
a programme being transmitted live is on air

explanation.surface: A polished society girl presenting a live programme.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Deb' is short for debutante, a young woman formally presented to high society.
explanation.definitionFit: A debonair person is confident, charming and stylish, smooth in manner.

clue.text: Arab or Irish-American on QI

parts.note: IR is the abbreviation for Irish and A for American
the letters as written, the name of a TV quiz show

explanation.surface: An Irish-American appears as a guest on the TV quiz show QI.
explanation.walkthrough: QI is a British TV panel quiz show; here its letters are taken as they stand.
explanation.definitionFit: Most people of Iraq are Arabs, so a native of that country fits as an example.

clue.text: See 6
Vote against elevating good, positive principle

indicators.note: in a down clue, raising a word means writing it upwards, backwards

parts.note: nay is a vote against

explanation.surface: Opposing a motion that would promote the good.
explanation.walkthrough: 'elevating' in a down clue lifts the vote upwards, so it reads backwards; yang is the partner of yin.
explanation.definitionFit: In Chinese philosophy this is the active, bright, masculine force paired with yin.

clue.text: Quarrel with boss to make this point

parts.note: a quarrel is a crossbow bolt, a kind of arrow
the head is the boss of an organisation

explanation.surface: Arguing with the boss to make one's point.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Quarrel' looks like an argument but is an archaic word for a crossbow bolt.
explanation.definitionFit: The sharpened tip fixed to a shaft is the pointed end of the missile.

clue.text: Woman in cold sea turned back

parts.note: C is the abbreviation for cold, as on taps

indicators.note: the sea's name is turned around, read backwards

parts.note: the Aral Sea in Central Asia

explanation.surface: A woman swimming in a cold sea turns back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turned back' reverses the name of the Aral Sea, the shrinking inland sea between Kazakhstan and Uzbekistan.
explanation.definitionFit: A female given name, as of the pianist Schumann, fits a generic woman.

clue.text: Enigma resolved with elder's magical skill

indicators.note: a resolved puzzle has been worked out and its parts sorted, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: the word elder; the 's stands for 'is', a link to what follows

explanation.surface: An old man's magic tricks solve a mystery.
explanation.walkthrough: 'resolved' rearranges ENIGMA with ELDER; the 's reads as 'is', a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Sleight of hand is the conjuror's art of deceiving the eye, a conjuring dexterity.
